cities.base: South Bank or Covent Garden, central for Tower, Westminster and the museums
cities.name: London

cities.base: near the city centre, walkable to the Baths and Pulteney Bridge
cities.name: Bath

cities.base: day trip from Bath, no overnight
cities.name: the Cotswolds (Bourton-on-the-Water, Bibury, Castle Combe)

cities.base: near the castle, a quiet final-night stop close to Heathrow
cities.name: Windsor

places.name: Churchill War Rooms
places.note: The underground bunker rooms are kept as they were, better than it sounds if you think you're museumed out

places.name: Roman Baths
places.note: The plumbing and the mosaics are still intact enough to make the two thousand years feel real.

places.name: London Eye
places.note: Overpriced for thirty minutes and a view you get free from a dozen bridges.

places.name: Churchill War Rooms
places.note: A short walk from the Abbey, the underground bunker rooms are the real draw.

places.name: British Museum
places.note: Free and open till 5pm most days, but it deserves more time than most people give it.

places.name: Borough Market
places.note: Good for a fast, real lunch between the Tower and the Museum, not a sit-down meal.

places.name: Tower of London
places.note: Book ahead, the crowds at the door in high season eat into your afternoon.

places.name: Thermae Bath Spa
places.note: Actual working thermal spa with a rooftop pool, the only place you can bathe in Bath's waters today since the Roman Baths themselves are not for swimming

places.name: Legoland Windsor
places.note: Skip unless travelling with young children specifically for this. It eats an entire day and is a taxi ride out of town, which does not fit a half day Heathrow buffer itinerary.

places.name: Windsor Royal Shopping (old station arcade)
places.note: Victorian train shed converted into a shopping arcade right by the castle, decent for a coffee or last minute gifts while waiting for a train back to Heathrow.

places.name: Cote Brasserie Windsor
places.note: Reliable French-style chain brasserie, fine for a low-stress dinner near the castle before an early Heathrow departure the next day. Nothing special but consistent.

places.name: The Two Brewers
places.note: Old pub right by the Long Walk entrance to the Great Park, solid pub lunch, gets busy on weekends. No under 18s inside which surprises some visitors.

places.name: Windsor Farm Shop
places.note: Small farm shop supplying produce from the royal estate, good for picking up local cheese or a snack, not a full meal stop. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Windsor Guildhall
places.note: Wren-associated town hall in the centre, where Prince Charles married Camilla civilly. Exterior only really, quick look on the way past.

places.name: French Brothers River Cruise
places.note: Short Thames cruise past the castle and Eton, runs frequently in season. Not a highlight but an easy low-effort way to see the castle from the water if you have a spare 40 minutes.

places.name: Thames Path Riverside Walk
places.note: Flat easy walk along the river with views up to the castle walls, connects to Eton bridge. Pleasant rather than essential, good for filling half an hour after lunch.

places.name: Windsor Great Park
places.note: Vast former royal hunting ground, the Long Walk runs straight from the castle for 2.65 miles to the Copper Horse statue. Free to walk, deer sometimes visible, good if the castle interior is closed.

places.name: Eton College and Eton High Street
places.note: Ten minute walk over the Thames footbridge from Windsor. The college itself has limited public access, but the high street with its old shopfronts is worth the stroll even from the outside.

places.name: Windsor Castle
places.note: Largest inhabited castle in the world, State Apartments and St George's Chapel included, but closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays much of the year so check before you build a half day around it. Changing of the Guard happens some mornings, worth timing for.

places.name: Cotswold Motoring Museum
places.note: Small collection of vintage cars and rural bygones, including the original Brum car from the children's TV show. Pleasant enough on a rainy morning but with only one day in the region this loses out to the villages themselves.

places.name: Cotswolds coach tour souvenir shops (Bourton high street)
places.note: Rows of fudge and souvenir shops aimed squarely at coach parties. Fine for a five minute browse if you're already there, not a reason to add time to the day.

places.name: Lower Slaughter
places.note: A short drive from Bourton, a stream lined by a mill and stone cottages with none of the crowd. If the day's schedule has any slack this is a better payoff per minute than a second hour in Bourton.

places.name: By Brook footpath, Castle Combe
places.note: Short streamside path just outside the village centre, an easy way to stretch legs away from the coach tour crowds clustered on the main street.

places.name: St Andrew's Church, Castle Combe
places.note: 13th century church with a faceless medieval clock, one of the oldest working clocks in England still in original condition. Quiet, free, worth the five minute look if the church is open.

places.name: Castle Combe Village
places.note: Honey stone cottages, a 14th century market cross, and no visible modern signage anywhere, which is why it keeps getting used as a film set (War Horse, Wolf Man, Stardust). Small enough to see on foot in under an hour.

places.name: The Swan Inn, Bibury
places.note: Riverside pub in the middle of the village, decent spot for a pub lunch if the day's itinerary allows a sit-down stop rather than grabbing something quick.

places.name: Bibury Trout Farm
places.note: Working trout farm right on the River Coln, you can feed the fish and buy smoked trout to take away. A quick, low key stop next to Arlington Row, not essential.

places.name: Arlington Row, Bibury
places.note: A row of 17th century weavers' cottages, one of the most photographed streets in England and the reason Bibury is on every itinerary. Narrow lane, no parking right at it, and it gets thick with photographers by late morning.

places.name: Birdland Park and Gardens
places.note: Penguins and flamingos among 500 birds in a riverside garden. Good if travelling with kids, skippable otherwise given the tight day.

places.name: The Model Village, Bourton-on-the-Water
places.note: A 1:9 scale replica of the village itself built in the 1930s, in the garden of the Old New Inn. Fun for ten minutes, not worth a detour on its own.

places.name: Bourton-on-the-Water River Walk
places.note: The River Windrush runs shallow through the village with low stone footbridges every few dozen feet, easy 20 minute stroll end to end. Gets crowded with coach tours by midday so go early.

places.name: Fashion Museum Bath
places.note: Closed permanently as a standalone venue after 2023, collection now in storage pending a new home, do not route people here

places.name: Alexandra Park
places.note: Best skyline view over the whole city, a stiff walk up from the centre but far fewer people than the Crescent

places.name: The Pump Room Restaurant
places.note: Grand Georgian room attached to the Roman Baths, live trio plays some days, food is fine not exceptional, you are paying for the room

places.name: Guildhall Market
places.note: Small covered market with a cafe counter, good for a quick cheap bite between sights

places.name: Sally Lunn's Eating House
places.note: Oldest house in Bath, famous for its Bath bun, a bit of a tourist trap but the basement kitchen museum is a nice add for £3

places.name: The Circus
places.note: Circular Georgian square by the same architect family as the Crescent, on the walk between the two

places.name: No. 1 Royal Crescent
places.note: Restored Georgian townhouse museum, gives context to why the Crescent looks the way it does, skippable if short on time

places.name: Royal Crescent
places.note: Georgian terrace of 30 houses, sweeping lawn out front, no ticket needed to see it from outside

places.name: Pulteney Bridge
places.note: One of few bridges in the world lined with shops on both sides, best view is from the weir below not on the bridge itself

places.name: Roman Baths
places.note: Well preserved Roman bathing complex, audio guide included, gets crowded by midday so go right at opening

places.name: Hyde Park
places.note: Free, big enough to actually clear your head after a train or a museum, Serpentine and Kensington Gardens are attached to it

places.name: Covent Garden
places.note: Street performers and stalls, fine for an hour if it's on the way, mostly a shopping arcade now rather than a real market

places.name: National Gallery
places.note: Free, good rainy day option if you want a second museum without paying, Van Gogh and Turner rooms are the draw

places.name: London Eye
places.note: 30 minutes for the view and a long queue, the same skyline is free from Waterloo Bridge or the Sky Garden

places.name: Soho
places.note: Dense with bars, restaurants, and theatres, good for wandering without a plan after a full day of sights

places.name: Tower Bridge Exhibition
places.note: Glass floor walkway, skippable if money's tight since the bridge is free to look at and walk across from outside

places.name: Tower of London
places.note: Crown Jewels and the Beefeater tour are worth the early start, book timed entry ahead or you queue

places.name: British Museum
places.note: Free, huge, the Rosetta Stone and Parthenon marbles are the ones people actually come for, do not try to see all of it

places.name: Borough Market
places.note: Good for a stand-up lunch between Tower and British Museum, gets packed by 12:30 so go early or after 2

places.name: Windsor Castle
places.note: A good half-day stop on the way to Heathrow if you want more than just a hotel night.

places.name: Royal Crescent
places.note: Georgian terrace curve, best seen on the walk down from the Crescent lawn.

places.name: Pulteney Bridge
places.note: One of the few bridges anywhere lined with shops, no ticket needed.

outings.why: The crown jewels and the medieval walls in one go, book ahead or queue at the door.
outings.name: Tower of London and Tower Bridge

outings.why: Free, vast, and open till 5pm most days, so it slots in after a Borough Market lunch.
outings.name: British Museum
outings.fallback: National Gallery, also free, if the queues or the crowds put you off.

outings.why: The Abbey is closed some Sundays for services, so check ahead; the War Rooms are a short walk after.
outings.name: Westminster Abbey and Churchill War Rooms

outings.why: The baths themselves are the point, the Abbey next door is a five-minute add-on.
outings.name: Roman Baths and Bath Abbey

outings.why: Hired car or tour, 7-8 hours door to door; the tiny lanes make self-drive slower than it looks but tours run £80-100pp.
outings.name: Cotswolds day: Bourton-on-the-Water, Bibury, Castle Combe

outings.why: No ticket needed, a loop through Bath's set-piece Georgian streets before the train back.
outings.name: Pulteney Bridge and Royal Crescent walk

outings.why: A half-day option on the way to Heathrow if you have the time and don't just want a hotel night.
outings.name: Windsor Castle
outings.fallback: Skip it and go straight to a Heathrow hotel for zero stress.

destination.name: England (London, Bath & Cotswolds)
destination.pitch: A proper London city break with a stone-village-and-Roman-baths detour, not a grand tour of the country.
destination.caveat: This is a lot of train logistics for seven days, and jet lag on day 2 will make the Tower/Museum day feel rushed. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: London is one of the great world cities and three nights is the minimum to do it properly.
because.food: Borough Market and Bath's cafes are solid, though this isn't a food-focused trip.
because.nature: The Cotswolds day gets you stone villages and green lanes, not wilderness.
because.culture: Tower of London, Westminster Abbey, British Museum and Roman Baths cover two thousand years without leaving the itinerary.
